questions.question: What does the wildcard ? extends T allow in a method parameter?
options: Inserting and reading elements of type T
explanations: With ? extends T you cannot insert (except null).
Correct. ? extends T (covariance) allows reading elements as type T, but not inserting.
You cannot insert, only read.
You can read elements and work with them.

questions.question: Which principle summarizes when to use ? extends T vs ? super T?
explanations: DRY is about not repeating code, not about generics.
Correct. PECS: Producer Extends (read-only), Consumer Super (write-only).
SOLID is a set of OOP design principles.
KISS is about general simplicity.

questions.question: Why can't you create a generic array like new T[10]?
options: Due to type erasure: arrays have a reified type
Because Java does not support arrays
Because new T[10] is invalid syntax
explanations: It is not related to the constructor.
Correct. Arrays know their type at runtime (reified), but generics use type erasure, so they are incompatible.
Java does support arrays.
The syntax new T[10] is not valid, but the underlying reason is type erasure.

questions.question: Which Collections.copy() method signature demonstrates the PECS pattern?
options: copy(List<? extends T> src, List<? super T> dest)
copy(List<? super T> src, List<? extends T> dest)
explanations: Without type parameters there is no safety.
Correct. src produces elements (? extends T), dest consumes elements (? super T).
It only allows copying between lists of the exact same type.
Reversed: src must be Producer Extends, dest Consumer Super.

questions.question: What is the main criticism of Java's generics implementation?
options: They use type erasure instead of reification
They do not allow multiple parameters
They only work with JDK classes
explanations: Performance is not a significant criticism.
Correct. Type erasure prevents reflection on generic types and creates incompatibility with arrays. .NET implements reification, which preserves types at runtime.
They do allow multiple parameters: Map<K, V>.
They work with any class.
